title: Pilot study on feasibility and safety of oral drinking trials in children with endotracheal intubation
summary: Mechanical ventilation with intubation is an integral part of pediatric intensive care. Because drinking while lying down with a tube in place is considered to carry a risk of choking or inhaling fluid, patients are fed only through a feeding tube and do not receive any fluids to drink. Older patients report feeling very thirsty after treatment. This study investigates whether independent drinking can be carried out safely and without increased risk despite intubation.
conditions: PICU-treatment, mechanical ventilation with endotracheal intubation, risk of aspiration

interventions.name: Drinking trial with 3-5 ml per kg Body weight of blue colored water
Application of 3-5 ml per kg Body weight of blue colored water by gastric tube

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation 
Comfort-B >12
protective reflexes intact
for children <2 years of age: gestational age at birth at least 36 weeks
Exclusion criteria:
Dysphagia
Pneumonia
lack of parental consent
